([[Middletown, Delaware]]) | college = [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] (2019–2021) | highlights = * [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2021) * Atlantic 10 All-Rookie Team (2020) }} '''Nah'Shon Lee "Bones" Hyland''' (born September 14, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]]. ==Early life and high school career== Hyland started playing basketball after watching his older brother, Tykee, playing at the park. He was nicknamed "Bizzy Bones" or "Bones" in part due to his slender build.{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's next star, 'Bones' Hyland carries his hometown of Wilmington on his back |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/vcus-next-star-bones-hyland-carries-his-hometown-of-wilmington-on-his-back/article_5208556b-e00c-5383-b9ad-cc0128b688d1.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=January 4, 2020}} Hyland attended [[St. Georges Technical High School]] in [[Middletown, Delaware]]. During his junior year, his 11-month-old cousin and grandmother died in a [[house fire]].{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=A year after a tragic fire, high-major recruit Nah'Shon Hyland has his groove back |url=https://theathletic.com/957786/2019/05/02/a-year-after-a-tragic-fire-high-major-recruit-nahshon-hyland-has-his-groove-back/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=May 2, 2019}} Hyland escaped by jumping from his second-floor bedroom and suffered a torn patellar tendon, sidelining him for six months.{{cite web |last1=Grube |first1=Ryan |title=After a life-altering house fire, Bones Hyland draws strength from losses |url=https://commonwealthtimes.org/2019/10/22/after-a-life-altering-house-fire-bones-hyland-draws-strength-from-losses/ |website=[[The Commonwealth Times]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=October 22, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 26.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 3.4 steals per game, leading his team to the semifinals of the state tournament. He was named Delaware Player of the Year and earned first team All-State honors.{{cite web |last1=Myers |first1=Brad |title=St. Georges' Hyland is Player of the Year, heads All-State boys basketball team |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/15/nahshon-hyland-heads-delaware-all-state-boys-basketball-team/3177572002/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=March 15, 2019}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] over offers from [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]], [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]], [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] and [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]].{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU adds four-star guard Nah'Shon Hyland to 2019 recruiting class |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-commonwealth-university/vcu-adds-four-star-guard-nahshon-hyland-to-2019-recruiting-class/article_c26b130a-2a0e-5a9d-a3fe-55c797c173e4.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=June 4, 2019}} ==College career== On January 18, 2020, Hyland scored a freshman season-high 21 points and five three-pointers in a 91–63 win over [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]].{{cite web |last1=Jeter |first1=Fred |title=VCU's Nah'Shon Hyland: A freshman with impact |url=http://richmondfreepress.com/news/2020/jan/31/vcus-nahshon-hyland-freshman-impact/ |website=[[Richmond Free Press]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=January 31, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged nine points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game, earning [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team accolades. He shot 43.4 percent from three-point range and set a program freshman record with 63 three-pointers.{{cite web |title=Nah'Shon Hyland |url=https://vcuathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/nah-shon-hyland/3653 |website=Virginia Commonwealth University |access-date=December 7, 2020}} In his sophomore season debut on November 25, Hyland scored 23 points, making five three-pointers, in an 85–69 victory over [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Marc |title=Hyland, Williams, strong finish propel VCU past Utah State |url=https://www.nbc12.com/2020/11/26/hyland-williams-strong-finish-propel-vcu-past-utah-state/ |website=[[WWBT]] |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}} On December 9, he scored 30 points, shooting 7-of-12 from three-point range, in a 95–59 win over [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].{{cite web |title=Hyland erupts for 30, Rams throttle Aggies |url=https://vcuathletics.com/news/2020/12/9/mens-basketball-hyland-erupts-for-30-rams-throttle-aggies.aspx |website=Virginia Commonwealth University |access-date=December 12, 2020 |date=December 9, 2020}} Six days later, Hyland posted a career-high 31 points in a 93–68 victory over [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Hyland scores 31 to lift VCU over Western Carolina 93-68 |url=https://www.si.com/college/college-basketball/game/2285367 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=December 15, 2020}} On March 5, 2021, he recorded 30 points and 10 rebounds in a 73–68 win against [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] at the [[2021 Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Tournament|Atlantic 10 Tournament]] quarterfinals.{{cite web |title=Hyland scores 30 to lift VCU past Dayton 73-68 in A-10 |url=https://apnews.com/article/basketball-hason-ward-jordy-tshimanga-jalen-crutcher-adrian-baldwin-5cc97c43b4cc29b71cabc9cb9ff8cae7 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 5, 2021}} As a sophomore, Hyland averaged 19.5 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.9 steals per game, and was named [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's Bones Hyland named Atlantic 10's player of year |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcus-bones-hyland-named-atlantic-10s-player-of-year/article_33d52e7a-ab0d-5de3-a09f-bcfe17d5ac2e.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} On April 17, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Epps |first1=Wayne |title=VCU's Bones Hyland declares for NBA draft |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcus-bones-hyland-declares-for-nba-draft/article_88d5fd70-207e-5609-bfb9-136fc41874a8.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]
